subject: Redwood Private VPC - competitive/networking follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@cloudops.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Private VPC - post-call recap and next tests

Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so the team is aligned: 

- Key requirements you called out:
  - Fully private deployment (no customer data to public endpoints unless explicitly allowed).
  - Air-gapped or restricted egress for highly regulated workloads.
  - Tight networking controls (private subnets, control-plane reachability constraints, KMS/HSM integration).
  - Evaluate performance and unit economics vs the hyperscaler inference API you currently use.

- Redwood differentiation (high level):
  - Private deployment modes (managed control plane with VPC peering OR customer-managed control plane for air-gapped installs).
  - Smart routing and cost controls to reduce per-token unit economics vs general-purpose cloud endpoints.
  - Ops tooling for rollouts, model pinning, and streaming telemetry for latency/cost breakdowns.

Attachments: Redwood_vs_Hyperscalers_1pager.pdf, Private_VPC_Networking_Checklist.xlsx (network checklist is the best place to start).

Proposed next tests (we recommend running these in parallel over the next 2 weeks):
1) Networking test: confirm whether outbound control-plane connectivity is acceptable, validate port/proxy requirements from your infra (owner: Rafael).
2) Control plane evaluation: show both managed-control-plane path (lighter ops, needs outbound) and customer-managed-control-plane path (air-gap friendly) and the install/config differences (owner: Camila).
3) Competitive perf/cost: small perf test against your current hyperscaler endpoint (3 models, 200 requests each) to compare latency, throughput, and per-token cost (owner: Camila).

Would you be available for a 30-45 min technical session Wednesday or Thursday to kick off the networking test? I can loop Rafael and Vanessa on the call.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@cloudops.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:27:35 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private VPC - post-call recap and next tests

Thanks Camila — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the networking call: 

1) For the managed control plane option, does Redwood require persistent outbound HTTPS to your control plane (i.e., do agents/call-home patterns exist)? If so, which FQDNs/IP ranges and ports are needed?
2) For the customer-managed control plane, can you confirm that all data plane traffic (inference requests/responses) can remain fully inside our VPC with no egress?
3) KMS integration: we need confirmation that Redwood can integrate with our AWS KMS/CloudHSM for model keys and log encryption (no key export).

Also please confirm whether the networking checklist includes a minimal set of firewall rules and NAT/proxy guidance - our infra team will need those to triage.

If you can send those details I'll propose a time for Wednesday afternoon.

Best,
Alice
VP Product, AcmeHealth
alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@cloudops.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Private VPC - post-call recap and next tests

Thanks — quick answers to Alice's questions and proposed owners: 

1) Managed control plane connectivity
   - Yes: the managed control plane uses outbound HTTPS (port 443) to a small set of Redwood control-plane FQDNs. We provide a published list of FQDNs/IP ranges and an option to restrict via mutual TLS for additional security. Owner: Rafael will share the exact allowlist.

2) Customer-managed control plane (air-gapped friendly)
   - Confirmed: with the customer-managed control plane install, you can run a control plane inside your VPC (or air-gapped environment) and there is no required outbound egress for inference/data traffic. Control-plane-only installs require one-time package transfer for initial install if fully air-gapped (we support air-gap install media + offline KMS handshake).

3) KMS/HSM
   - We integrate with AWS KMS and can support CloudHSM-backed keys. No key material is exported by Redwood - we rely on KMS APIs or HSM-backed providers (we also support customer-managed key proxies for fully isolated setups).

4) Networking checklist
   - The attached Private_VPC_Networking_Checklist.xlsx includes a minimal firewall/NAT/proxy matrix (egress/ingress, ports 80/443 for control plane, optional service ports for observability, recommended CIDR ranges). Rafael will add entries for mutual TLS endpoints and any vendor-specific ports.

Suggested immediate plan:
- Rafael: share allowlist + port checklist in the next 24 hours.
- Camila: schedule Wednesday 3pm PT technical kickoff (networking + control-plane options).
- Vanessa: prepare short demo showing managed vs customer-managed control plane differences and a one-page PoC plan for perf tests.
